::: {.bnr-manual-flag .bnr-manual-flag--technical}
Technical Manual
:::

## What this page does

Use this page to preview, review and deploy a public Info-Hub website change.

The sequence is: edit locally → render locally → review the exact changes → push a development branch → merge it into `main` on GitHub → check the deployed website.

A successful Stata publication does not deploy the website. A successful local Quarto render does not make a change live.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Procedure at a glance"}
1. Start the local editing session.
2. Pull `main` and create a development branch.
3. Edit, preview and complete a local render.
4. Inspect, commit and push only the intended public files.
5. Merge the pull request into `main`, then check GitHub Actions and the live site.
:::

## Before you start

Confirm that the workstation is set up, the required analytical data package or report is already approved and published, and all files proposed for Git are suitable for the public repository.

`main` is the protected publication branch. Do routine work on a development branch. A merge into `main` triggers GitHub Pages deployment.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Input files

| File or source | What to check |
|---|---|
| Intended changed QMD, configuration or public asset | It is the correct public source file and belongs to the task. |
| Approved files in `site/downloads/` or another website mirror | If the task includes analytical content, only approved public copies are present. |
| VS Code Source Control changes list | No private data, credentials, local configuration or unrelated files are proposed for commit. |
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Code and configuration files

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `start-info-hub-edit.bat` | Opens VS Code, starts the local preview and opens Firefox. Run directly by double-clicking it from the repository root. |
| `site/_quarto.yml` | Controls the Quarto site, including the pre-render Downloads catalogue builder. |
| `.github/workflows/publish-site.yml` | GitHub Actions controller that renders and deploys the site after `main` changes. It is called automatically by GitHub. |
| `requirements.txt` | Python packages installed by GitHub Actions before rendering. Do not change it for an ordinary content update. |
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Output files

| File or folder | Result |
|---|---|
| `site/_site/` | Generated local website. Review it but do not edit or commit it. |
| `site/downloads/downloads.yml` | Generated central Downloads catalogue. It changes only when the approved catalogue records change; do not edit it by hand. |
:::

## Step 1: Start the editing session

At the repository root, double-click:

`start-info-hub-edit.bat`

It checks the repository, site configuration and Python environment; opens the repository in VS Code; starts a **BNR info-hub Quarto Preview** Command Prompt; and opens `http://127.0.0.1:4200/` in Firefox.

Keep the preview Command Prompt open while editing. Closing it stops the preview. The launcher does not choose a branch, update Git, commit, publish or deploy anything.

## Step 2: Update `main` and create a development branch

In VS Code:

1. Click the branch name in the lower-left status bar and select `main`.
2. Open **Source Control**, select `...`, then select **Pull**.
3. When Pull completes, click the branch name again and select **Create new branch**.
4. Enter a short descriptive name, for example `update-annual-report`.

The lower-left status bar should show your new branch name. Do not edit directly on `main`.

The equivalent commands, entered in a **VS Code PowerShell terminal** opened with **Terminal > New Terminal**, are:

```powershell
git switch main
git pull origin main
git switch -c update-annual-report
```

Replace `update-annual-report` with your own short branch name. The final command reports that it has switched to the new branch.

## Step 3: Edit and preview

Make the required public source change in VS Code and save it. The local preview should refresh in Firefox.

Check the changed page, new or amended links, tables, figures, downloads and navigation. For detailed content-editing guidance, use [Update website content](update-content.qmd).

## Step 4: Run a complete local render

Open a new **VS Code PowerShell terminal**. At the repository root, enter:

```powershell
.\venv-info-hub\Scripts\Activate.ps1
cd site
quarto render
```

The render runs the Downloads catalogue builder, then refreshes `site/_site/`. It is successful when it completes without an error message. Inspect the affected pages and any linked listing, download or navigation element before committing.

## Step 5: Inspect the files to commit

In VS Code Source Control, read the complete **Changes** list. Open each important file to inspect its before-and-after comparison.

Stage only the intended public files. Do not commit generated `site/_site/` output, confidential data, tokens, private review files or unrelated local changes.

The equivalent check in a VS Code PowerShell terminal is:

```powershell
git status
git diff
```

`git status` should list only the files that belong to your task.

## Step 6: Commit and push the development branch

In VS Code Source Control:

1. Click `+` beside each intended file.
2. Enter a short commit message.
3. Select **Commit**.
4. Select **Publish Branch** or **Push**.

The branch is now on GitHub, but the public website has not changed.

The equivalent commands are:

```powershell
git add site/path/to/changed-file.qmd
git commit -m "Describe the website change"
git push -u origin update-annual-report
```

Replace the file path and branch name with your own. `git push` should report the new remote branch and its pull-request URL.

## Step 7: Merge the pull request on GitHub

Open the [BNR Info-Hub repository](https://github.com/UWI-BNR/info-hub){target="_blank"}.

1. Open **Pull requests** and select **New pull request**.
2. Set **base** to `main` and **compare** to your development branch.
3. Review the changed files and complete any required team review.
4. Select **Merge pull request** when the change is ready.

Only this merge changes `main` and starts website deployment. After the merge, update your local `main` next time by pulling from GitHub; do not push directly to protected `main`.

## Step 8: Confirm deployment and check the live site

On GitHub, open **Actions** and select the newest **Publish Quarto site** run. Confirm that both **build** and **deploy** completed successfully.

Then open the [public Info-Hub](https://uwi-bnr.github.io/info-hub/){target="_blank"} and check the affected pages. For a data-package release or report publication, also check the expected dashboard, table or report page, download link, Downloads catalogue entry and any affected listing.

The task is complete only after the live website is correct.
